orig_ds: External Carotid Artery and Facial nerve only
new_ds: Radial nerve and Brachial artery, associated vessels, and surrounding connective fascia
External Carotid Artery and Facial nerve only, associated vessels, and surrounding connective fascia
Femoral nerve and Iliac artery, associated vessels, and surrounding connective fascia

questionText: The Kidney of the adult domestic Ox (Bovine) is anatomically unique among domestic mammals because it is:
c: Externally Lobated (multilobed) with 15 to 25 distinct superficial lobes, and lacks a renal pelvis
orig_ds: Smooth and unipyramidal with a renal pelvis
new_ds: Smooth and unipyramidal with a renal pelvis
Smooth multipyramidal situated along the course of the regional vascular network
Heart-shaped situated along the course of the regional vascular network

questionText: In the equine kidney, the renal pelvis and terminal collecting ducts are histologically unique because they contain:
c: Mucus-secreting tubuloalveolar glands (glandulae pelvis renalis), which make normal equine urine thick, cloudy, and viscous
new_ds: Abundant stratified squamous epithelium, associated vessels, and surrounding connective fascia
No mucus glands, associated vessels, and surrounding connective fascia
Heavy calcification in all nephrons, associated vessels, and surrounding connective fascia

questionText: The glans penis of the adult Boar (Sus scrofa) is pathognomonic for having a:
c: Spiral, corkscrew-shaped terminal twist that locks into the interdigitating pulvini cervicales of the sow's cervix
orig_ds: Bulbus glandis that causes a coital tie
new_ds: Long vermiform appendage situated along the course of the regional vascular network
Massive mushroom-shaped flare situated along the course of the regional vascular network
Bulbus glandis that causes a coital tie

questionText: In the female bovine reproductive tract, the internal endometrium bears permanent, button-like, avascular-appearing aglandular elevations termed 'Caruncles', which are:
c: Convex in the Cow, but Concave (cup-shaped) in the Ewe

questionText: The Cervix of the Sow (female pig) differs from that of the cow and mare because its cervical canal features:
c: Interdigitating rounded mucosal prominences (Pulvini cervicales) that occlude the lumen like a zipper, and lacks a distinct fornix vaginae
orig_ds: 3 to 4 circular rigid annular rings with a deep fornix
new_ds: Total absence of muscularis situated along the course of the regional vascular network
3 to 4 circular rigid annular rings with a deep fornix

questionText: The 'Moderator Band' (Septomarginal Trabecula / Trabecula septomarginalis) is a muscular-tendinous cord traversing the lumen of which cardiac chamber to conduct electrical impulses?
c: Right Ventricle (connecting the interventricular septum to the base of the parietal wall / anterior papillary muscle)

questionText: The 'Cisterna Chyli' (the dilated abdominal receiving reservoir for lymph from the pelvis, hindlimbs, and viscera that gives rise to the Thoracic Duct) is located dorsal to the aorta at the level of:
c: L1 to L4 (between the crura of the diaphragm)
new_ds: T5 to T7 (T5 to T7 variant)
C6 to C7 (C6 to C7 variant)

questionText: In bovine meat inspection, the 'Prefemoral Lymph Node' (Subiliac lymph node) is routinely palpated and incised on the carcass at the cranial border of the:
c: Tensor fasciae latae muscle, in the fold of the flank

questionText: The portal vein (Vena portae) transports nutrient-rich blood from the digestive viscera to the liver, formed by the convergence of which three major veins?
c: Splenic vein, Cranial Mesenteric vein, and Caudal Mesenteric vein (and Gastroduodenal vein)
orig_ds: Renal vein, Hepatic vein, and Femoral vein
new_ds: Renal vein, Hepatic vein, and Femoral vein (collateral anatomical structure)
Jugular vein and Subclavian vein (collateral anatomical structure)
Azygos vein and Iliac vein (collateral anatomical structure)

questionText: Cranial Nerve I (Olfactory nerve) fibers pass from the olfactory neuroepithelium into the olfactory bulbs through which perforated bony plate?
c: Cribriform plate of the Ethmoid bone

questionText: The Optic Nerve (Cranial Nerve II) exits the cranial vault through which bony canal?
c: Optic Canal (Canalis opticus) of the Presphenoid bone

questionText: The Hypoglossal Nerve (Cranial Nerve XII) exits through the hypoglossal canal and provides motor innervation to:
c: All intrinsic and extrinsic muscles of the Tongue (styloglossus, hyoglossus, genioglossus)
new_ds: Muscles of mastication (Muscles of mastication variant)

questionText: The 'Horner's Syndrome' in dogs, cats, and horses (characterized by miosis, ptosis, enophthalmos, and protrusion of the third eyelid) results from disruption of the:
c: Oculosympathetic (cervical sympathetic) pathway

questionText: In cattle, Caudal Epidural Anesthesia is routinely performed by inserting a spinal needle into which intervertebral space?
c: First Intercoccygeal space (between Coccygeal 1 and Coccygeal 2) or the Sacrococcygeal space (S5-Co1)
new_ds: Lumbosacral space (L6-S1) situated along the course of the regional vascular network

questionText: Lumbosacral Epidural Anesthesia in the Dog and Sheep is performed by needle puncture into the epidural space between:
c: Lumbar 7 (L7) and Sacral 1 (S1) vertebrae

questionText: Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF) is collected in horses and cattle from the Cisterna Magna (cerebellomedullary cistern) at which anatomical landmark?
c: Atlanto-Occipital Space (articulation between the occipital condyles and the atlas)
new_ds: Between thoracic spines (Between thoracic spines variant)

questionText: The Pudendal Nerve (Nervus pudendus) innervates the caudal external genitalia, and in the bull, Pudendal Nerve Block is performed to achieve:
c: Relaxation and desensitization of the retractor penis muscle, allowing protrusion and examination of the penis
new_ds: Flank desensitization situated along the course of the regional vascular network
Ruminal atony situated along the course of the regional vascular network

questionText: The 'Jugular Furrow' (sulcus jugularis) of the horse and ox, accommodating the external jugular vein for routine venipuncture, is bounded ventrally by which muscle?
c: Sternocephalicus muscle (specifically the sternomandibularis in ox and horse)

questionText: Which of the following cartilages is completely devoid of a perichondrium, relying solely on surrounding synovial fluid or adjacent tissues for its nutrition?
c: Fibrocartilage (e.g., intervertebral discs and pelvic symphysis)

questionText: In mammalian skeletal muscle fibers, a 'Triad' observed at the junction of the A and I bands is anatomically composed of:
c: One central transverse tubule (T-tubule) flanked by two terminal cisternae of the sarcoplasmic reticulum
orig_ds: One T-tubule and one sarcoplasmic reticulum cisterna (Dyad)
Two T-tubules and one terminal cisterna
new_ds: One T-tubule and one sarcoplasmic reticulum cisterna (Dyad)
Three adjacent myofibrils situated along the course of the regional vascular network
Two T-tubules and one terminal cisterna

questionText: In neuronal cytology, the basophilic clumps known as 'Nissl bodies' (Nissl substance) correspond ultrastructurally to:
c: Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER) and polyribosomes (absent in the axon and axon hillock)
new_ds: Golgi apparatus complexes (Golgi apparatus complexes variant)
Neurofilaments and microtubules (Neurofilaments and microtubules variant)

questionText: In the domestic Ox and Sheep, the outer adrenal cortex (zona subcapsularis) exhibits cellular cords arranged in arched or loop-like clusters, earning it the histological designation:
c: Zona arcuata (characteristic of carnivores and equines, whereas ruminants display rounded clusters as classic Zona glomerulosa)
new_ds: Zona fasciculata (Cortical intermediate zone synthesizing glucocorticoid cortisol)
Zona reticularis (Deep cortical zone synthesizing adrenal androgens)

questionText: Avian lungs differ fundamentally from mammalian lungs because they are non-collapsible, constant-volume structures where gas exchange occurs in tubular:
c: Parabronchi (Air capillaries) with unidirectional airflow
orig_ds: Terminal blind alveoli with tidal airflow
new_ds: Terminal blind alveoli with tidal airflow

questionText: How many total air sacs (sacci pneumatici) are typically present in the domestic fowl (Gallus domesticus)?
c: 9 (1 single interclavicular, 2 cervical, 2 cranial thoracic, 2 caudal thoracic, and 2 abdominal)
